about: Modellbildung und Simulation (ModSim), FH Technikum Wien master's programme, 2nd semester: the eight worked lecture examples of Puhwein (2021a) and the 13 tasks of the task sheet Puhwein (2021b), animated step by step, each step with the MATLAB that gives its result. Equations and results from the worked examples, cited by PDF page as 'VO p. N' (transcribed in docs/sources/vo-solutions-a.md and -b.md); the two-mass values from the TM3 note 'Bestimmung der Eigenfrequenzen des 2DoF Systems' (Zusatz Material, 'TM3 note'). The task-sheet labs have no solution sheet and are worked here. tests/unit/labs-data.test.js recomputes every practice answer with the core.

labs.title: Single-mass oscillator (Ein-Massen-Schwinger)
labs.idea: Cut the mass free, write the forces into Newton's law, solve for ẍ, and you have both the ODE and the Simulink model: one Integrator per dot.
labs.law: m ẍ + c ẋ + k x = F₁(t)

equations.eq: ẍ = F₁/m − (c/m)(ẋ − ẋ₀) − (k/m)(x − x₀)
equations.note: The DGL in the form for Simulink; the time plot integrates it with x₀ = ẋ₀ = 0

equations.eq: ω₀ = √(k/m), f₀ = ω₀/2π, T₀ = 1/f₀
equations.note: Natural frequency of the undamped linear system

equations.eq: ω_D = √(ω₀² − (c/2m)²)
equations.note: Damped natural frequency
State space, x₁ = x, x₂ = ẋ, u = F₁

practice.question: m = 2 kg, k = 800 N/m: what is ω₀?
practice.source: VO p. 7: ω₀ = √(k/m); values chosen here

practice.question: With c = 8 N·s/m as well, what is ω_D?
practice.source: VO p. 8: ω_D = √(ω₀² − (c/2m)²)

labs.title: Pendulum (Pendel)
labs.idea: Build T, V and D, apply Lagrange's operator, and the pendulum's ODE appears; then see where sin φ ≈ φ stops being true and which rest angles are stable.
labs.lecture: Puhwein (2021a), example 2, VO pp. 2, 10–18; Wagg and Neild (2015) for the stability chart
labs.law: m L₁² φ̈ + c_D φ̇ + k_D φ + m g L₁ sin φ = −M₁(t)

equations.eq: d/dt ∂L/∂q̇ − ∂L/∂q + ∂D/∂q̇ = Q
equations.note: Lagrange's equations of the 2nd kind with a dissipation function, L = K − V

equations.eq: φ̈ = [−M₁ − m g L₁ sin φ − k_D φ − c_D φ̇]/(m L₁²)
equations.note: The nonlinear model the swing plots

equations.eq: φ̈ + c_D/(mL₁²) φ̇ + (g/L₁ + k_D/(mL₁²)) φ = −M₁/(mL₁²)
equations.note: Linearised with sin φ ≈ φ: the faint pendulum

equations.eq: ω₀ = √(g/L₁), T₀ = 2π√(L₁/g)
equations.note: Small swings without spring

equations.eq: J = [0 1; −ω² cos x₁ −δ]
equations.note: Jacobian; at 2nπ stable spirals (light damping), at (2n+1)π saddles

practice.question: L₁ = 1 m, g = 9.80665 m/s²: how long is one small swing, T₀?
practice.source: VO p. 11: ω₀ = √(g/L₁)

labs.title: Pendulum with roller (Pendel mit Rolle)
labs.idea: A rod with a rolling disc at its end, held up by a spring: the spring's length follows from the geometry, the disc's spin from rolling, and both go into one Lagrange equation.
labs.lecture: Puhwein (2021a), example 3, VO pp. 3, 19–24, after Fotiu (2018a)
labs.law: (m₁L₁²/3 + (3/2)m₂L₁²) φ̈₁ = (m₁/2 + m₂) g L₁ cos φ₁ − k(S − l₀) dS/dφ₁

equations.eq: S(φ₁) = √({L₁[1 − cos φ₁]}² + [L₂ + L₁ sin φ₁]²)
equations.note: Spring length; the sheet writes 0.25 for L₂

equations.eq: K = ½[(m₁L₁²/3)φ̇₁² + m₂(L₁φ̇₁)² + (m₂r²/2)(L₁φ̇₁/r)²]
equations.note: Kinetic energy of rod and rolling disc

equations.eq: V = −m₁g(L₁/2) sin φ₁ − m₂gL₁ sin φ₁ + ½k(S − l₀)²
equations.note: Gravity and spring

equations.eq: (m₁L₁²/3 + (3/2)m₂L₁²) φ̈₁ = (m₁/2 + m₂) g L₁ cos φ₁ − k(S − l₀) dS/dφ₁
equations.note: The lab's equation, from K and V of pp. 22–23; the sheet prints (3/2)m₂r and a spring moment without L₁ (README)

equations.eq: (m₁L₁²/3 + (3/2)m₂r) φ̈₁ − (m₂ + m₁/2) g L₁ cos φ₁ + k(S − l₀)(2 sin φ₁ + cos φ₁)/(4S) = 0
equations.note: The sheet's printed equation, run faint beside the lab's

practice.question: With the lab's starting values (m₁ = 1 kg, m₂ = 0.5 kg, k = 200 N/m, l₀ = 0.25 m, L₁ = 0.5 m, L₂ = 0.25 m), at what angle φ₁ does the rod rest?
practice.source: worked here: the moment of the lab's equation set to zero
practice.solution: (m₁/2 + m₂) g L₁ cos φ₁ = k(S − l₀) dS/dφ₁ at φ₁ ≈ 5.6°.

labs.title: Two-mass oscillator (Zwei-Massen-Schwinger)
labs.idea: Two masses give two coupled ODEs, M ẍ + C ẋ + K x = F; det(K − λM) = 0 gives two eigenfrequencies, each with its own way of moving.
labs.lecture: Puhwein (2021a), example 5, VO pp. 4, 27–31; values from the TM3 note, pp. 1–2
labs.law: M ẍ + C ẋ + K x = F

equations.eq: ẍ₁ = (1/m₁)[F₁ − c₁ẋ₁ − k₁x₁ + c₂(ẋ₂ − ẋ₁) + k₂(x₂ − x₁)], ẍ₂ = (1/m₂)[F₂ − c₂(ẋ₂ − ẋ₁) − k₂(x₂ − x₁)]
equations.note: The form for Simulink (x₀ = ẋ₀ = 0); the driven run integrates it

equations.eq: M = [m₁ 0; 0 m₂], C = [c₁+c₂ −c₂; −c₂ c₂], K = [k₁+k₂ −k₂; −k₂ k₂]
equations.tex: M = \begin{bmatrix} m_1 & 0 \\ 0 & m_2 \end{bmatrix}, \; C = \begin{bmatrix} c_1+c_2 & -c_2 \\ -c_2 & c_2 \end{bmatrix}, \; K = \begin{bmatrix} k_1+k_2 & -k_2 \\ -k_2 & k_2 \end{bmatrix}
equations.note: Mass, damping and stiffness matrices

equations.eq: det(K − λM) = 0, λ = ω₀ᵢ²
equations.note: The eigenvalue problem; the modes step animates its eigenvectors

equations.eq: λ₁,₂ = tr/2 ∓ √((tr/2)² − det), of M⁻¹K
equations.note: The same λ from trace and determinant of M⁻¹K

equations.eq: (K − ω²M + jωC) X = F̂
equations.note: Frequency response, plotted as |x₁/F₁| like the TM3 note's bode

practice.question: m₁ = m₂ = 1 kg, k₁ = 2000 N/m, k₂ = 750 N/m: what is the first eigenfrequency f₀₁?
practice.solution: λ from det(K − λM) = 0: 500 and 3000 s⁻²; √500/2π = 3.559 Hz.

practice.question: And the second, f₀₂?
What is the smaller λ = ω² of eig(K,M) there?
practice.source: TM3 note p. 2: EW = diag(500, 3000)

labs.title: Double pendulum (Doppelpendel)
labs.idea: Two hinged rods: Lagrange gives two coupled nonlinear ODEs; two runs a thousandth of a radian apart soon have nothing in common, yet each keeps its energy.
labs.lecture: Puhwein (2021a), example 6, VO pp. 4, 32–40, after Fotiu (2018a, 2018b)
labs.law: (8/3)φ̈₁ + φ̈₂ cos(φ₂−φ₁) − φ̇₂² sin(φ₂−φ₁) + 3(g/L₁) sin φ₁ = 0

equations.eq: (2/3)φ̈₂ + φ̈₁ cos(φ₂−φ₁) + φ̇₁² sin(φ₂−φ₁) + (g/L₁) sin φ₂ = 0
equations.note: The second equation; with the first, the chaos step integrates both

equations.eq: K = (mL₁²/6)[4φ̇₁² + φ̇₂² + 3φ̇₁φ̇₂ cos(φ₂ − φ₁)]
equations.note: Kinetic energy; the energy step plots K + V

equations.eq: V_g = −(mgL₁/2) cos φ₁ − mgL₁[cos φ₁ + ½ cos φ₂]
equations.note: Potential energy of gravity

equations.eq: V_F = ½k_D(φ₂ − φ₁)², D = ½c_D(φ̇₂ − φ̇₁)²
equations.note: Torsion spring and damper at A; in the equations divided by mL₁²/2 they enter as 2k_D/(mL₁²) and 2c_D/(mL₁²)
Linearised at φ₁ = φ₂ = 0, whose eigenmodes the last step shows

practice.question: L₁ = 1 m, no spring: what is the lower linear eigenfrequency ω₁?
practice.source: worked here from VO p. 34's linearised equations: det(K̃ − λM̃) = 0

labs.title: RLC circuit (Elektrischer Schwingkreis)
labs.idea: The mesh rule with i = q̇ gives the single mass's ODE in other letters; the energy moves between capacitor and coil while the resistor turns it to heat.
labs.lecture: Puhwein (2021a), example 4, VO pp. 3, 25–26, after Nemecek (2014)
labs.law: L q̈ + R q̇ + q/C = u(t)

equations.note: The form for Simulink; the energy step integrates it

equations.eq: ω₀ = 1/√(LC)
equations.note: Natural angular frequency

equations.eq: ½Li², q²/(2C), ∫Ri² dt
equations.note: Energy in the coil, in the capacitor, and turned to heat: the bars

practice.question: L = 0.1 H, C = 1 mF: what is ω₀?
practice.source: VO p. 26: ω₀ = 1/√(LC)

labs.title: DC motor (E-Motor)
labs.idea: The armature circuit and the shaft are two ODEs coupled by k_M and k_T: the current turns the shaft and the turning shaft pushes the current back.
labs.law: u_A = R_A i_A + L_A di_A/dt + k_M ω,  J φ̈ + c_L φ̇ = k_T i_A
labs.lawTex: u_A = R_A i_A + L_A\frac{\mathrm{d}i_A}{\mathrm{d}t} + k_M\omega, \quad J\ddot{\varphi} + c_L\dot{\varphi} = k_T i_A

equations.eq: di_A/dt = (1/L_A)[u_A − R_A i_A − k_M ω], φ̈ = (1/J)[k_T i_A − c_L ω − M_L]
equations.tex: \frac{\mathrm{d}i_A}{\mathrm{d}t} = \frac{1}{L_A}[u_A - R_A i_A - k_M\omega], \quad \ddot{\varphi} = \frac{1}{J}[k_T i_A - c_L\omega - M_L]
equations.note: The form for Simulink; M_L the Simulink model's load torque, not in the sheet's ODE

equations.eq: ω∞ = (k_T u_A − R_A M_L)/(R_A c_L + k_M k_T)
equations.tex: \omega_\infty = \frac{k_T u_A - R_A M_L}{R_A c_L + k_M k_T}
equations.note: Speed at rest, from both equations with the derivatives zero

equations.eq: u_A i_A = R_A i_A² + k_T i_A ω + d/dt(½L_A i_A²)
equations.tex: u_A i_A = R_A i_A^2 + k_T i_A\omega + \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left(\frac{1}{2}L_A i_A^2\right)
equations.note: Power balance of the circuit (k_M = k_T in SI units): the bars

practice.question: u_A = 12 V, R_A = 1 Ω, k_M = k_T = 0.05, c_L = 10⁻³ N·m·s/rad, no load: what speed ω does the motor reach?
practice.source: worked here from VO p. 42 with the derivatives zero

labs.title: Electromechanical shaker
labs.idea: A coil in a magnet pushes a sprung plate: a circuit in series with a single-mass oscillator, and, if the coil's motion is let back into the circuit, a slower current.
labs.lecture: Puhwein (2021a), example 8, VO pp. 5, 43–45, after Nemecek (2014)
labs.law: U_S = R_S i_S + L_S di_S/dt,  m_S ẍ + d_S ẋ + k_S x = h_S i_S
labs.lawTex: U_S = R_S i_S + L_S\frac{\mathrm{d}i_S}{\mathrm{d}t}, \quad m_S\ddot{x} + d_S\dot{x} + k_S x = h_S i_S

equations.eq: G_Ux(s) = 1/(R_S + sL_S) · h_S/(m_S s² + d_S s + k_S)
equations.tex: G_{Ux}(s) = \frac{1}{R_S + sL_S}\cdot\frac{h_S}{m_S s^2 + d_S s + k_S}
equations.note: Displacement over voltage

equations.eq: A = [−R_S/L_S 0 0; 0 0 1; h_S/m_S −k_S/m_S −d_S/m_S]
equations.note: State space (i_S, x, v), back-EMF left out: the uncoupled current

equations.eq: L_S di_S/dt = U_S − R_S i_S − h_S ẋ
equations.note: With the back-EMF: the coupled current

practice.question: U_S = 4 V, R_S = 4 Ω, h_S = 5 N/A, k_S = 2000 N/m: how far does the plate move at rest, in metres?
practice.source: worked here from VO p. 43 with the derivatives zero

labs.title: Task 2: pendulum on a sprung block (Pendel mit Federaufhängung)
labs.idea: No solution sheet; worked here. A block on a vertical spring carries a pendulum: two coordinates, one T, one V, and the two coupled equations the group derived in 2021.
labs.lecture: Puhwein (2021b), task 2, p. 1; the group's report (Baghdadi, Keck and Maurer 2021) for the values
labs.law: m_ges ÿ − m_s l₁(θ̈ sin θ + θ̇² cos θ) + c ẏ + k y − m_ges g = F₁
labs.lawTex: m_{ges}\ddot{y} - m_s l_1(\ddot{\theta}\sin\theta + \dot{\theta}^2\cos\theta) + c\dot{y} + ky - m_{ges}g = F_1

equations.eq: I θ̈ − m_s l₁ ÿ sin θ + m_s g l₁ sin θ + c_T θ̇ + k_T θ = M₁
equations.tex: I\ddot{\theta} - m_s l_1\ddot{y}\sin\theta + m_s g l_1\sin\theta + c_T\dot{\theta} + k_T\theta = M_1
equations.note: The pendulum's equation; with the block's, the motion step integrates both. m_s = m₁/2 + m₃, I = l₁²(m₁/3 + m₃)

equations.eq: y* = m_ges g/k
equations.note: Rest position of the block

equations.eq: M = [m_ges 0; 0 I], K = [k 0; 0 m_s g l₁ + k_T]
equations.tex: M = \begin{bmatrix} m_{ges} & 0 \\ 0 & I \end{bmatrix}, \quad K = \begin{bmatrix} k & 0 \\ 0 & m_s g l_1 + k_T \end{bmatrix}
equations.note: Linearised at the rest: block and pendulum uncoupled, the modes step

practice.question: With the group's values (m₁ = m₂ = m₃ = 0.1 kg, k = 10 N/m), how far below the relaxed spring does the block rest?
practice.source: worked here; the group's report p. 8 gives y = m_ges g/k

practice.question: And the pendulum's linear eigenfrequency, with l₁ = 0.2 m and k_T = 40 N·m/rad?
practice.source: worked here: √((m_s g l₁ + k_T)/I)/2π

labs.title: Task 3: horizontally excited pendulum
labs.idea: No solution sheet; worked here. The same block and pendulum lying on the floor: now the block's motion swings the pendulum even at rest, so the two modes stay coupled.
labs.law: m_ges ẍ + m_s l₁(θ̈ cos θ − θ̇² sin θ) + c ẋ + k x = F₁
labs.lawTex: m_{ges}\ddot{x} + m_s l_1(\ddot{\theta}\cos\theta - \dot{\theta}^2\sin\theta) + c\dot{x} + kx = F_1

equations.eq: I θ̈ + m_s l₁ ẍ cos θ + m_s g l₁ sin θ + c_T θ̇ + k_T θ = M₁
equations.tex: I\ddot{\theta} + m_s l_1\ddot{x}\cos\theta + m_s g l_1\sin\theta + c_T\dot{\theta} + k_T\theta = M_1
equations.note: The pendulum's equation; the motion step integrates both

equations.eq: M = [m_ges m_s l₁; m_s l₁ I], K = [k 0; 0 m_s g l₁ + k_T]
equations.tex: M = \begin{bmatrix} m_{ges} & m_s l_1 \\ m_s l_1 & I \end{bmatrix}, \quad K = \begin{bmatrix} k & 0 \\ 0 & m_s g l_1 + k_T \end{bmatrix}
equations.note: Linearised at x = 0, θ = 0: coupled through M

practice.question: With the lab's starting values (masses 0.1 kg, l₁ = 0.2 m, k = 10 N/m, k_T = 0.1 N·m/rad), what is the lower eigenfrequency?
practice.source: worked here: det(K − λM) = 0

labs.title: Task 5: quarter car under road excitation
labs.idea: No solution sheet; worked here. A wheel and a body on two springs: the road moves the tyre spring's foot, and the body follows slow roads and ignores fast ones.
labs.law: m₁ẍ₁ + c₁(ẋ₁ − ẇ) + k₁(x₁ − w) − c₂(ẋ₂ − ẋ₁) − k₂(x₂ − x₁) = 0

equations.eq: m₂ẍ₂ + c₂(ẋ₂ − ẋ₁) + k₂(x₂ − x₁) = 0
equations.note: The body; with the wheel's, the response step integrates both

equations.eq: w(t) = ŵ₀ cos(Ωt)
equations.note: The road, as the sheet writes it

equations.eq: (K − ω²M + jωC) X = [k₁ + jωc₁; 0] ŵ₀
equations.note: The transmissibility |x₂/ŵ₀| plotted

practice.question: Wheel 40 kg, body 300 kg, tyre 200 kN/m, suspension 20 kN/m: what is the body's (lower) eigenfrequency?
practice.source: worked here: det(K − λM) = 0; example values
practice.solution: λ₁ = 60.5 s⁻², √60.5/2π = 1.24 Hz (the wheel hops at 11.8 Hz).

labs.title: Task 6: two-disc torsional oscillator (2DoF Torsionsschwinger)
labs.idea: No solution sheet; worked here. Two discs on a shaft are the two-mass oscillator turned: J for m, torsion springs for springs, angles for positions.
labs.law: J₁φ̈₁ + c_T1(φ̇₁ − ẇ) + k_T1(φ₁ − w) − c_T2(φ̇₂ − φ̇₁) − k_T2(φ₂ − φ₁) = M₁
labs.lawTex: J_1\ddot{\varphi}_1 + c_{T1}(\dot{\varphi}_1 - \dot{w}) + k_{T1}(\varphi_1 - w) - c_{T2}(\dot{\varphi}_2 - \dot{\varphi}_1) - k_{T2}(\varphi_2 - \varphi_1) = M_1

equations.eq: J₂φ̈₂ + c_T2(φ̇₂ − φ̇₁) + k_T2(φ₂ − φ₁) = M₂
equations.note: The second disc; the response step integrates both, driven by w, M₁ and M₂

equations.eq: M₁(t) = M₀₁ cos(Ω₁t), M₂(t) = M₀₂ cos(Ω₂t)
equations.tex: M_1(t) = M_{01}\cos(\Omega_1 t),\; M_2(t) = M_{02}\cos(\Omega_2 t)
equations.note: The torques on J₁ and J₂, as drawn, each at its own frequency (phases φ₁, φ₂ taken 0)

equations.eq: w(t) = ŵ₀ cos(Ωt)
equations.note: The shaft end's angle, as the sheet writes it

equations.eq: (K − ω²M + jωC) X = [k_T1 + jωc_T1; 0] ŵ₀
equations.note: The transmissibility |φ₂/ŵ₀| plotted

practice.question: J₁ = 0.02, J₂ = 0.05 kg·m², k_T1 = 50, k_T2 = 80 N·m/rad: what is the lower eigenfrequency?
practice.source: worked here: det(K − λM) = 0; example values

labs.title: Task 7: hanging two-mass chain, shaken at the top
labs.idea: No solution sheet; worked here. Measured from the static rest, the weight drops out and the hanging chain is the quarter car upside down.
labs.law: m₁ẍ₁ + c₁(ẋ₁ − ẇ) + k₁(x₁ − w) − c₂(ẋ₂ − ẋ₁) − k₂(x₂ − x₁) = 0

equations.eq: m₂ẍ₂ + c₂(ẋ₂ − ẋ₁) + k₂(x₂ − x₁) = 0
equations.note: The lower mass; the response step integrates both

equations.eq: w(t) = ŵ₀ cos(Ωt)
equations.note: The suspension point, as the sheet writes it

equations.eq: (K − ω²M + jωC) X = [k₁ + jωc₁; 0] ŵ₀
equations.note: The transmissibility |x₂/ŵ₀| plotted

practice.question: With the TM3 note's masses and springs (1 kg, 1 kg, 2000 N/m, 750 N/m), what is the higher eigenfrequency of the hanging chain?
practice.source: worked here; the same K and M as the TM3 note p. 1, so its f0_2 = 8.7173 Hz
practice.solution: The same matrices as the lying two-mass oscillator: gravity only shifts the rest.

labs.title: Task 1: elastic pendulum
labs.idea: No solution sheet; worked here. A block on a spring–damper rod: read as fixed to the rod (2 degrees of freedom, r and φ), it bounces and swings at once, and near a 2 : 1 ratio the two trade energy. Every number is an example value — not given on the sheet.
labs.law: m₁r̈ − m₁rφ̇² − m₁g cos φ + k(r − l₀) + c ṙ = 0
labs.lawTex: m_1\ddot{r} - m_1 r\dot{\varphi}^2 - m_1 g\cos\varphi + k(r - l_0) + c\dot{r} = 0

equations.eq: (m₁r² + J₁)φ̈ + 2m₁rṙφ̇ + m₁g r sin φ + k_T φ + c_T φ̇ = M₁
equations.tex: (m_1 r^2 + J_1)\ddot{\varphi} + 2m_1 r\dot{r}\dot{\varphi} + m_1 g r\sin\varphi + k_T\varphi + c_T\dot{\varphi} = M_1
equations.note: The swing; the motion step integrates both

equations.eq: ω_r = √(k/m₁), ω_φ = √((m₁g r* + k_T)/(m₁r*² + J₁)), r* = l₀ + m₁g/k
equations.tex: \omega_r = \sqrt{k/m_1},\quad \omega_\varphi = \sqrt{\frac{m_1 g r^* + k_T}{m_1 r^{*2} + J_1}},\quad r^* = l_0 + \frac{m_1 g}{k}
equations.note: Linear at rest the two part

practice.question: With the lab's example values (m₁ = 1 kg, a 0.10 m × 0.06 m block, l₀ = 0.5 m, k = 200 N/m, k_T = 0), at what frequency does the pendulum swing at small angles?
practice.source: worked here: ω_φ² = m₁g r*/(m₁r*² + J₁); example values

labs.title: Task 4: unbalance-excited oscillator
labs.idea: No solution sheet; worked here. Two masses stacked on springs, a rod turned at a prescribed speed Ω on the lower one: the unbalance pushes with (m₃/2 + m₄)l₃Ω² cos Ωt. 2 degrees of freedom, since the rod's angle is driven. Every number is an example value — not given on the sheet.
labs.law: (m₁+m₃+m₄)ÿ₁ + c₁ẏ₁ + k₁y₁ − c₂(ẏ₂−ẏ₁) − k₂(y₂−y₁) = −(m₃/2 + m₄)l₃Ω² cos Ωt

equations.eq: m₂ÿ₂ + c₂(ẏ₂ − ẏ₁) + k₂(y₂ − y₁) = 0
equations.note: The upper mass; the motion step integrates both

equations.eq: β(t) = Ωt
equations.note: The rod's angle, driven: Ω(t) read as a prescribed speed

practice.question: With the lab's example values (m₁ = 2 kg, m₂ = 1 kg, m₃ = 0.1 kg, m₄ = 0.05 kg, k₁ = 2000 N/m, k₂ = 750 N/m), what is the lower eigenfrequency?
practice.source: worked here: det(K − λM) = 0 with M = diag(m₁+m₃+m₄, m₂); example values

labs.title: Task 8: coupled pendulums
labs.idea: No solution sheet; worked here. Two pendulums joined by a spring–damper, each rod read as two segments m, l (the sheet's double label): started alone, one passes its swing to the other and back. Every number is an example value — not given on the sheet.
labs.law: J₁φ̈₁ + 2g l₁(m₁+m₃) sin φ₁ + k_T φ₁ + c_T φ̇₁ + [k(S − b) + cṠ] ∂S/∂φ₁ = M₁
labs.lawTex: J_1\ddot{\varphi}_1 + 2g l_1(m_1+m_3)\sin\varphi_1 + k_T\varphi_1 + c_T\dot{\varphi}_1 + [k(S - b) + c\dot{S}]\,\partial S/\partial\varphi_1 = M_1

equations.eq: J₂φ̈₂ + 2g l₂(m₂+m₄) sin φ₂ + k_T φ₂ + c_T φ̇₂ + [k(S − b) + cṠ] ∂S/∂φ₂ = M₂
equations.tex: J_2\ddot{\varphi}_2 + 2g l_2(m_2+m_4)\sin\varphi_2 + k_T\varphi_2 + c_T\dot{\varphi}_2 + [k(S - b) + c\dot{S}]\,\partial S/\partial\varphi_2 = M_2
equations.note: The second pendulum; the motion step integrates both

equations.eq: S = √[(b + l₂ sin φ₂ − l₁ sin φ₁)² + (l₁ cos φ₁ − l₂ cos φ₂)²]
equations.note: The spring's length, exact

practice.question: With the lab's example values (segments 0.05 kg and 0.25 m, end masses 0.5 kg, k = 20 N/m, k_T = 0), at what frequency do the pendulums swing against each other?

labs.title: Task 9: two rolling discs
labs.idea: No solution sheet; worked here. Two discs rolling without slipping, tied to the wall and to each other at their axles: rolling adds half of each disc's mass again. Every number is an example value — not given on the sheet.
labs.law: (3/2)m₁ẍ₁ + c₁ẋ₁ + k₁x₁ − c₂(ẋ₂ − ẋ₁) − k₂(x₂ − x₁) = M₁/r₁

equations.eq: (3/2)m₂ẍ₂ + c₂(ẋ₂ − ẋ₁) + k₂(x₂ − x₁) = F₁
equations.note: Disc 2; the motion step integrates both

equations.eq: M₁(t) = M₀₁ cos(Ωt), F₁(t) = F₀₁ cos(Ωt)
equations.tex: M_1(t) = M_{01}\cos(\Omega t),\quad F_1(t) = F_{01}\cos(\Omega t)

labs.title: Task 10: two rolling discs, held at the rim
labs.idea: No solution sheet; worked here. As task 9, but the wall spring holds the top of disc 1's rim, which moves twice as far as the axle: the spring acts four times as stiff. Every number is an example value — not given on the sheet.
labs.law: (3/2)m₁ẍ₁ + 4c₁ẋ₁ + 4k₁x₁ − c₂(ẋ₂ − ẋ₁) − k₂(x₂ − x₁) = M₁/r₁

equations.eq: (3/2)m₂ẍ₂ + c₂(ẋ₂ − ẋ₁) + k₂(x₂ − x₁) = F₁
equations.note: Disc 2; the motion step integrates both

equations.eq: V₁ = ½k₁(2x₁)²

labs.title: Task 11: roller pendulum, held at the rim
labs.idea: No solution sheet; worked here. A pendulum hanging from the axle of a rolling disc, the disc held at the top of its rim: task 3's pendulum on a block, with a rolling disc for the block. Every number is an example value — not given on the sheet.
labs.law: (3/2 m₁ + m₂)ẍ + m₂l(φ̈ cos φ − φ̇² sin φ) + 4cẋ + 4kx = F₁ + M₁/r

equations.eq: m₂l²φ̈ + m₂lẍ cos φ + m₂g l sin φ = 0
equations.tex: m_2 l^2\ddot{\varphi} + m_2 l\ddot{x}\cos\varphi + m_2 g l\sin\varphi = 0
equations.note: The pendulum; the motion step integrates both

equations.eq: M = [3/2 m₁ + m₂  m₂l; m₂l  m₂l²], K = [4k 0; 0 m₂g l]
equations.tex: M = \begin{bmatrix} \tfrac{3}{2}m_1 + m_2 & m_2 l \\ m_2 l & m_2 l^2 \end{bmatrix},\quad K = \begin{bmatrix} 4k & 0 \\ 0 & m_2 g l \end{bmatrix}

labs.lawTex: a_{11}\ddot{\varphi}_1 + b\cos(\varphi_2-\varphi_1)\ddot{\varphi}_2 - b\dot{\varphi}_2^2\sin(\varphi_2-\varphi_1) + G_1\sin\varphi_1 + k_1\varphi_1 - k_2(\varphi_2-\varphi_1) + c_1\dot{\varphi}_1 - c_2(\dot{\varphi}_2-\dot{\varphi}_1) = M_1 - M_2
